title: Free vs Paid Walking Tour in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **A free walking tour is a tip-based tour.** You pay nothing upfront and decide at the end. Operators in Berlin say most guests give between €10 and €50 per person.
**Standard paid public tours cost about €20 to €28 per adult** for two to three and a half hours, and their stated maximums are 20, 25 or 30 people.
**Only a stated cap makes a tour small.** Tours that put a number in writing cap at 8 to 15 people. Two listings with Small Group in the title allow 20 and 25.

**Group size changes what reaches you.** In a group of 10 the last person stands about 2.4 m from the guide. In a group of 35 the back row is about 5.1 m away and hears the guide roughly 11 decibels quieter.
**Choose the tip-based tour** if your budget is tight, you decide on the day, or you want the famous first-day route past the Brandenburg Gate.
**Choose a small paid group** if you ask questions, travel with parents or children, or want a confirmed place at a fixed time.
**My own walk, Berlin Then and Now:** €25 per person, no more than 10 people, 12:30 from the World Clock on Alexanderplatz to Hackescher Markt, about 2.5 hours, with an archive photo at every stop.
